subject: Discovery Recap: Observability & Evals - AlliedCare
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Jamie Torres <jamie.torres@alliedcare.com>
Cc: rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai, neha.kapoor@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 15:02:00 -0800
Subject: Discovery Recap: Observability & Evals - AlliedCare

Hi Jamie - thanks again for the intro call today. Quick recap from our side to make sure we captured the right pain, goals, and next steps. Please correct anything I missed.

Pain points you shared:
- Limited observability into inference quality regressions: when product QA flags an issue we can’t reliably map it to model changes or traffic/route differences.
- No standardized evals/golden prompts: teams run ad-hoc notebooks which makes regressions hard to reproduce.
- Lack of tracing hooks: it’s difficult to correlate API calls, prompt inputs, and downstream user issues (metadata, tenant id, feature flags).
- Rollout uncertainty: you don’t have automated rollback/guardrails for model rollouts (canary thresholds, regression alerts).

Current stack / constraints:
- Services on AWS EKS; inference currently goes through in-house proxies + SageMaker-hosted endpoints for some models.
- Using OpenAI for a subset of features; internal teams run manual evals in notebooks.
- 99th pctl latency target for product features is ~300ms; spikes are a concern during peak windows.

Success criteria you mentioned:
- Detect meaningful quality regressions within 24 hours of deployment (and alert the right owners).
- Correlate user-reported failures to model/version/route within the UI.
- Maintain 99th pctl latency < 300ms for critical flows.
- Safe rollout capability: canary with automatic rollback on regression SLOs.

What we can deliver quickly (next week):
- Sample observability dashboard (attached PDF) showing per-model/per-route latency, token cost, and a regression timeline tied to eval runs.
- Example tracing hook spec for request metadata (tenant id, request id, prompt hash) and where to inject traces in your proxy.
- Golden prompt seed set (attached .xlsx) proposal and a lightweight eval plan (metric definitions + pass/fail thresholds).

Requested next steps / asks:
1) Please confirm the list of attendees for a technical deep-dive (we suggested your infra + ML platform owner).
2) Share any internal SLO docs or a recent incident ticket that would help us model regression thresholds.
3) If you can, provide a short sample of anonymized request logs (1-2 days) so we can validate the tracing surface.

We’ll put together a short architecture sketch and a tentative eval schedule for the deep-dive next week (week of Nov 29).

Attachments: observability-dashboard-sample.pdf, golden-prompts.xlsx

Cheers,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Solutions | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai
---
Redwood Inference - developer-first inference platform: latency, cost, and reliability controls for LLM-powered products.

From: Jamie Torres <jamie.torres@alliedcare.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai, neha.kapoor@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 19 Nov 2026 09:14:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Discovery Recap: Observability & Evals - AlliedCare

Marissa - thanks for the thorough recap. This aligns closely with what we discussed. A few clarifications and additional context from our side:

- Traffic profile: ~120k inference calls/day across product and internal tooling; peak QPS ~220 during business hours.
- Teams: Product (Sophie), Platform (me), and ML Research (two engineers) will attend the deep-dive.
- What we need from Redwood specifically:
  * Tracing hooks that capture tenant_id, request_id, prompt_hash, model_version, and route.
  * Dashboards that combine latency, cost, and a rolling regression score (ideally tied to golden prompt pass rates).
  * A proposal for canary thresholds (we can start conservative).

Attachments: I’m attaching a short SLO excerpt that includes our existing latency targets and a sample incident report from last month - should help tune the detection windows.

Also: we can share anonymized logs but will need guidance on what fields to strip; Sophie will coordinate with you on that.

Thanks - Jamie
Jamie Torres
Head of Platform Engineering, AlliedCare
jamie.torres@alliedcare.com
Phone: (415) 555-0139

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Jamie Torres <jamie.torres@alliedcare.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: neha.kapoor@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 19 Nov 2026 15:40:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Discovery Recap: Observability & Evals - AlliedCare

Jamie - appreciate the details. Next steps from Redwood ops/solutions side: 

1) Technical deep-dive: propose Tue, Dec 1 @ 10am PT (60 min). Invite link: https://app.hubspot.com/meetings/alliedcare/tech-deep-dive
2) Pre-work (before Dec 1):
   - Sophie/Jamie: share anonymized sample logs (we’ll provide a scrub checklist).
   - AlliedCare: confirm which models you want in the initial eval (prod model + fallback variant).
   - Redwood: we’ll deliver the sample dashboard + tracing hook spec by Mon, Nov 29.
3) Eval plan (during Dec):
   - Week 1: run golden-prompt pass/fail evaluation across historical samples; compute baseline pass rate and per-prompt deltas.
   - Week 2: deploy canary (1% traffic) with regression alerts; measure pass-rate and latency delta; automatic rollback if pass-rate drops >X% (to be decided in deep-dive).

Links / references:
- Sample dashboard (drive): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-sample-dashboard
- HubSpot meeting link: https://app.hubspot.com/meetings/alliedcare/tech-deep-dive

I’ll also add a short checklist for required RBAC + logging access. Neha - can you own the dashboard build and drop the prototype to the Drive by Monday?

Thanks,
Rishi Malhotra
Director, Solutions Engineering | Redwood Inference

rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai

Sounds great - Tue Dec 1 @ 10am PT works for us. Attendees: Jamie, Sophie (platform), Rahul (ML research), plus 1 infra engineer. We’ll prepare a 1-2 day anonymized log sample and Sophie will coordinate RBAC/access with Neha.

One ask before the deep-dive: can you include an example of a regression alert notification (Slack/email) that ties back to the failing golden prompt and includes key metadata (tenant, model_version, request_id)? That will help our on-call routing.

Appreciate it - looking forward to the prototype.

- Jamie
